edges.description: Dense bilateral cataract deprives the developing visual system of form vision; delay of surgery during the first weeks of life costs acuity.

edges.source: Early cataract extraction with optical rehabilitation

edges.description: Like the human cataract 40 alleles, the Xcat lesion sits in intron 1 and changes Nhs transcription without truncating the coding sequence.
edges.limitations: The mouse lesion is an insertion that removes one isoform, whereas the human alleles are a duplication-triplication and a small intronic deletion whose effect on NHS expression has not been measured.

edges.description: Xcat lenses show fiber cell degeneration leading to total cataract.

nodes.description: The structural variants are proposed to disturb the regulation of NHS transcription. Intron 1 is unusually large and is retained at proportionally large size even in the compact Fugu genome, suggesting regulatory elements, and the mouse Xcat insertion in the same intron suppresses the isoform transcribed from exon 1. Patient NHS expression has not been measured, so the direction and tissue pattern of the change are unknown.

animal_models.description: Like the human cataract 40 alleles, the Xcat lesion sits in intron 1 and changes Nhs transcription without truncating the coding sequence.
animal_models.name: Xcat mouse

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: The hypothesis that intron 1 is important for transcriptional regulation is supported by the identification of the mutation in the Xcat mouse

evidence.reference_title: Xcat, a novel mouse model for Nance-Horan syndrome inhibits expression of the cytoplasmic-targeted Nhs1 isoform.
evidence.snippet: The insertion inhibits the expression of the Nhs1 isoform containing exon 1 and results in exclusive expression of the alternative isoform containing exon 1A. Quantitative RT-PCR of Xcat cDNA shows reduced levels of Nhs1 transcripts.

nodes.description: Deprivation amblyopia is the main determinant of long-term vision and depends on the age at cataract extraction.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital and infantile cataract: aetiology and management.
evidence.snippet: Despite early surgery and aggressive optical rehabilitation, children may still develop deprivation amblyopia, nystagmus, strabismus, and glaucoma.

nodes.description: Dense bilateral central (nuclear) cataracts in hemizygous males, present from birth and needing extraction in the first months of life.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: In brief, all affected males required cataract extraction in the first few months of life.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Non-syndromic X-linked congenital cataract is characterized by bilateral total nuclear cataract in affected males and Y-sutural opacities in carrier females

nodes.description: In the Xcat mouse, primary and then secondary lens fibers become disorganised and degenerate after their initial elongation, while the lens epithelium looks normal. NHS isoforms regulate actin remodelling through a WAVE homology domain and associate with epithelial junctions, which is the proposed link between altered NHS levels and fiber cell failure; that link has been shown in cultured cells, not in lens.

animal_models.description: Xcat lenses show fiber cell degeneration leading to total cataract.
animal_models.name: Xcat mouse

evidence.reference_title: Lens development in a dominant X-linked congenital cataract of the mouse.
evidence.snippet: The observed sequence of histological changes indicates that the Xcat mutation affects the differentiation of lens fiber cells at some point after their initial elongation.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic localization and phenotypic expression of X-linked cataract (Xcat) in Mus musculus.
evidence.snippet: the site of gene action for the Xcat locus is suggested to be endogenous to the lens cells

evidence.reference_title: The Nance-Horan syndrome protein encodes a functional WAVE homology domain (WHD) and is important for co-ordinating actin remodelling and maintaining cell morphology.
evidence.snippet: We show that NHS controls cell morphology by maintaining the integrity of the circumferential actin ring and controlling lamellipod formation.

nodes.description: Lens extraction within the first weeks of life, followed by aphakic optical correction and amblyopia treatment, is the only management; there is no NHS-directed therapy. Earlier surgery reduces deprivation amblyopia but is associated with more secondary membrane formation and glaucoma.
nodes.id: Early cataract extraction with optical rehabilitation

evidence.reference_title: Congenital and infantile cataract: aetiology and management.
evidence.snippet: Good outcomes have been reported in children undergoing surgery before 6 weeks of age in children with unilateral cataract and before 10 weeks of age in bilateral cases.

evidence.reference_title: The critical period for surgical treatment of dense congenital bilateral cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Deprivation amblyopia may be minimized with early surgery for bilateral cataracts.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we show that NHS and X-linked cataract are allelic diseases.

nodes.description: Copy number variants at Xp22.13 either duplicate and triplicate the whole NHS locus or delete part of its first intron, leaving the coding sequence intact.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: CXN was found to be caused by novel copy number variations: a complex duplication-triplication re-arrangement and an intragenic deletion, predicted to result in altered transcriptional regulation of the NHS gene.

nodes.description: A 4.8 kb deletion inside the roughly 350 kb first intron of NHS in a second CXN family (Family I), proposed to remove transcriptional regulatory sequence.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: Sequence analysis revealed a 4.8 kb deletion within the large (∼350 kb) intron 1 of the NHS gene

nodes.description: A complex rearrangement in the original four-generation CXN family (Family H): an approximately 0.5 Mb triplication encompassing NHS, SCML1 and RAI2 embedded in a larger duplication, segregating with all affected males and carrier females.

evidence.reference_title: X-linked cataract and Nance-Horan syndrome are allelic disorders.
evidence.snippet: A segmental duplication–triplication encompassing the NHS, SCML1 and RAI2 genes (0.8 Mb) was identified in Family H, and a 4.8 kb deletion in NHS intron 1 was identified in Family I.

nodes.description: Sensory nystagmus secondary to early visual deprivation.

evidence.reference_title: The critical period for surgical treatment of dense congenital bilateral cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Surgery after 4 weeks was associated with a greater prevalence of strabismus and nystagmus than surgery before 4 weeks

nodes.description: A spontaneous X-linked dominant cataract mutation caused by a large insertion between exons 1 and 2 of Nhs, which suppresses the exon 1 (cytoplasmic) isoform. Hemizygous males have complete penetrance and heterozygous females a variegated lens phenotype.
